To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a multilevel framework is necessary to understand how built environment features influence health outcomes, (b) the built environment is not the only determinant of physical activity and health outcomes, and (c) there are several statistical approaches available to analyze the data from cluster samples.
the built environment is associated with physical activity behavior and health outcomes.

(a) multilevel models are more appropriate than single-level models for analyzing the associations of built environment characteristics with physical activity and health outcomes; (b) the associations of built environmental characteristics with residents' physical activities and health outcomes vary by age, gender, ethnicity, and other sociodemographic and socioeconomic factors; and (c) the associations between built environment characteristics and residents' physical activity behaviors and health outcomes are mediated by residents' perceptions of the environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people use their environment and how this use is related to their health.
understanding how the physical activity environment affects the behavior and health of the people who live in it, and how the physical activity of the people who use the environment affects it.
the development and testing of a theory-based intervention to increase physical activity and improve health outcomes among low-income African American adults.

there is no single "best" approach for analyzing clustered data in studies exploring associations of built environment with physical activity and health outcomes.
the choice of a statistical approach depends on the research questions, the data, and the study's characteristics.
multilevel modeling is a powerful and flexible statistical tool to account for clustered data in cross-sectional studies.

the built environment has a significant impact on physical activity and health outcomes.

the choice of a statistical approach is important in studies of the built environment and health.
